stem: A client with stable chronic heart failure reports becoming fatigued while preparing meals and doing light household tasks. Which practical modification should the nurse recommend?

options.A: Sit during meal preparation or similar household tasks when helpful and schedule rest periods so routine activity is paced rather than completed in one prolonged effort.
options.B: Complete several household tasks while standing, then take one longer rest afterward so the client avoids interrupting each task and finishes the work sooner.
options.C: Limit household tasks to days when fatigue is absent and use rest instead of routine activity on days when tiredness develops during usual self-care.
options.D: Begin each household task while standing and switch to sitting only after fatigue develops so activity tolerance is challenged before the client rests.

rationale: The American Heart Association recommends scheduling daily rest and relaxation for people with heart failure so they do not overdo activity and specifically suggests sitting during household tasks such as preparing food or ironing. Regular physical activity should still be individualized to the client's heart health. Therefore A is correct because it combines practical activity modification with planned rest. B clusters exertion before resting, C replaces appropriate routine activity with unnecessary inactivity whenever fatigue occurs, and D delays the energy-conserving modification until after fatigue has already developed.
educational_objective: For a stable client with heart failure who becomes fatigued during household activities, use practical energy-conservation measures such as sitting for tasks and scheduling rest while maintaining appropriate individualized activity.
source_version_date: Current AHA resource; last reviewed June 16, 2025
source_locator: Get enough rest: schedule time every day for rest and relaxation; daytime rest can help prevent overdoing activity and ease tiredness; examples include putting the feet up periodically and sitting during household tasks such as preparing food or ironing. Be physically active: the amount and type of activity should depend on the client's heart health and individualized activity plan.
source_claim_supported: People with heart failure can conserve energy by scheduling daily rest and sitting during household tasks while continuing physical activity appropriate to their individualized heart-health plan.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed pp. 35–37: assess client performance of activities of daily living and assist when needed; provide information on adaptations for performing activities of daily living; Mobility/Immobility: assess mobility and implement measures to promote mobilization; Rest and Sleep: assess the client's sleep/rest pattern and schedule care activities to promote adequate rest.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — energy conservation during activities of daily living in heart failure
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four options to remove absolute-word cueing and the uniquely-long keyed answer while preserving the directly sourced heart-failure energy-conservation construct. The revised distractors use realistic errors in activity clustering, unnecessary inactivity, and delayed use of seated task modification.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Chronic heart failure — energy conservation during household activities
audit_findings.stem: PASS — stable heart-failure context and fatigue during routine household activity create a focused Basic Care and Comfort teaching task.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly reflects AHA guidance to sit during household tasks and schedule rest; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — standing for multiple tasks and postponing rest clusters exertion rather than conserving energy through pacing.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — temporary rest can be appropriate, but routinely replacing activity whenever fatigue occurs overrestricts a stable client's individualized activity.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — sitting is appropriate, but delaying the modification until after fatigue develops defeats the preventive energy-conservation strategy.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only option that proactively combines the two directly sourced strategies without adding a contradictory practice.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B clusters exertion, C promotes unnecessary inactivity, and D delays the supported modification until symptoms appear.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — all options are comparable in length and clinical detail and no keyed-only absolute wording remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort includes ADL adaptation, mobilization support, and interventions that promote adequate rest.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether delayed rest or activity avoidance could be defended as energy conservation; AHA specifically recommends planned rest and sitting during household tasks while maintaining individualized activity, leaving A uniquely best.
